title: Billing-Latency Causality Mapper & Compact Alert Digest
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a service in the console backend that automatically identifies not just outliers, but likely causal relationships between billing increases and latency regressions, and surface a compact, actionable alert digest to SREs and product owners.

Why: We routinely receive alerts that a tenant's bill rose or latency degraded, but the root cause is often correlated signals (e.g., sudden model variant change, batch size regressions, or query pattern shifts). Existing anomaly detectors flag individual signals but provide little causal context; responders spend time cross-referencing dashboards. This work reduces time-to-resolution and false-positive paging by bundling top causal contributors with a short remediation playbook.

Scope:
- Data sources: token billing events, per-tenant latency histograms, per-route model version and config metadata, autoscaling events, KV cache hit/miss rates, and recent deploy/rollout notes.
- Detection: compute correlation and causal scores using a lightweight ensemble (time-lagged cross-correlation, Granger-causality heuristic, and feature-transfer-shift scoring). Focus on intraday windows (1h/6h/24h) with fast incremental updates.
- Digest format: a one-paragraph summary + top 3 contributing signals with contribution percentages, a confidence score, suggested immediate mitigations (e.g., fallback to smaller model variant, pause burst routing, enable cache warmup), and links to prepopulated logs/dashboards/PRs.
- Integration: expose findings as structured alerts in the Console (per-tenant and global), attach to existing incident flow, and provide API endpoints so external runbooks can fetch the digest.

Acceptance criteria:
- Detects at least 85% of seeded causal scenarios in the staging generator suite (billing spike caused by tokenization bug, latency regression from large-batch rollout, cost increase from misconfigured caching TTL).
- Alert digest limited to 300 chars summary + up to 3 contributor lines and renders in the Console with direct links.
- False positive rate below 8% on historical baseline for last 90 days of production telemetry in evaluation.

Architecture notes:
- Backend service will run as a stateless aggregator with a small Redis-backed state for recent windowed aggregates. Heavy windowed computation (e.g., transfer entropy) can be handled by a separate batch job that writes candidate signals to a results topic (Kafka) consumed by the aggregator.
- Use existing telemetry pipeline (usage events + metrics ingestion) and reuse the console's metric-store read nodes for low-latency queries.
- Alerting: route high-confidence digests to PagerDuty for P0 escalations only; send low/medium confidence to a digest inbox and Slack channel. Configurable per-customer thresholds via Console.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement prototype detector with a single causality heuristic (lagged cross-correlation) behind a feature flag; validate on synthetic seeded tests.
2) Instrument digest rendering in Console as read-only for SREs (no paging).
3) Iterate on ensemble scoring and add remediation suggestions; run shadow alerts for two weeks against production telemetry.
4) Enable paging for high-confidence findings and open a post-rollout RCA.

Metrics to track: precision/recall on seeded scenarios, average time-to-identify, number of pager actions avoided, reduction in MTTR for billing/latency incidents.

Open trade-offs:
- Accuracy vs latency: heavier causal algorithms are more precise but increase pipeline latency — mitigate by running expensive models in batch and combining results.
- Tenant privacy: we must avoid exposing raw payloads in digests; only surface aggregated contributor labels and links that require Console auth.

Longer-term ideas: integrate with Optimize to automatically suggest quantization or batching profile changes when certain causal patterns recur.
